neighbours.label: the next item in a list of bodily symptoms or body movements (tremor, stiffness, postural instability; clapping and waving), as opposed to lists of objects
fire: Patients often describe dizziness, nausea and blurred vision after the fall.
Typical findings are drooling, slurred speech and postural sway.
The baby has begun kicking, rolling and reaching for toys.
Warning signs include chest pain, shortness of breath and sweating.
The dance teacher showed them stepping, hopping and swaying in time.
Her illness brought fatigue, muscle cramps, fever and hoarseness.
The monkey kept scratching and grimacing, hooting and shrieking.
Long-term effects can include twitching, memory loss and involuntary grunting.
quiet: Shoppers often buy bread, milk and fresh eggs after work.
Typical offerings are pasta, grilled fish and green salad.
The shop has begun selling kites, puzzles and wooden toys.
Useful items include a tent, a sleeping bag and matches.
The art teacher brought them paper, paint and brushes in boxes.
Her suitcase held socks, shirts, a map and sunglasses.
The garage kept ladders and buckets, hoses and shovels.
Later models can include heated seats, cruise control and a roof rack.

short: next item in a list of symptoms or body movements
notes: The card's peaks include ' to' in 'akin to' and ' as' in 'such as', which sit one step before the symptom. The label names the expected next item, not one token.
